```{r}
#| label: setup
library(knitr)
metrics <- read.csv("../results/model_metrics.csv")
fair <- read.csv("../results/fairness_audit.csv")
gaps <- read.csv("../results/fairness_gaps.csv")
verdicts <- jsonlite::read_json("../results/verdicts.json")
splitv <- jsonlite::read_json("../results/split_verification.json")
run <- jsonlite::read_json("../results/run_summary.json")
fmt <- function(x, d = 4) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d)
```

# Research question

Does an R-native rebuild of the credit-risk champion from the Python lab
`credit-risk-lab` (tidymodels: regularized logistic regression, gradient
boosting through the xgboost engine, plus a GAM arm) reproduce the Python
champion's discrimination on the same UCI Taiwan credit data and the same
locked split, and where do group fairness gaps (equal opportunity,
predictive parity) sit across sex, age bands, and education?

The study was pre-registered in `PREREGISTRATION.md`, committed before
any model was fit. Hypotheses, split, threshold, and verdict rules were
frozen there.

# Data and the locked split

Data: UCI dataset 350, "default of credit card clients" (Taiwan, 2005),
30,000 accounts, committed byte-identical in this repo (SHA-256 checked
by the pipeline). Loading, recodes, and feature engineering mirror
`credit-risk-lab` line for line.

The split is the Python lab's split: stratified 70/30,
`train_test_split(random_state = 42)`. It is replicated in pure R
(`R/sklearn_split.R`, a numpy-compatible MT19937 plus the
StratifiedShuffleSplit steps) and proven identical, not approximated:

```{r}
#| label: split-table
data.frame(
  quantity = c("train rows", "test rows", "test defaults",
               "test event rate", "test positions SHA-256 (R)",
               "reference SHA-256 (Python)", "identical"),
  value = c(splitv$n_train, splitv$n_test,
            splitv$n_test_per_class[[2]],
            fmt(splitv$test_event_rate, 5),
            splitv$r_test_positions_sha256,
            splitv$reference_test_positions_sha256,
            splitv$identical)
) |> kable()
```

# Arms and headline results

Arm 1 is ridge logistic regression (glmnet via tidymodels, penalty tuned
by 5-fold cross-validation on the training set only; chosen penalty
`r fmt(run$chosen_penalty_glmnet, 5)`). Arm 2 is gradient boosting with
the xgboost engine at the Python champion's hyperparameters (300 trees,
learning rate 0.06, depth 3). Arm 3 is a GAM fit directly with mgcv,
with smooth terms for the continuous features: full interpretability is
its purpose.

```{r}
#| label: metrics-table
metrics$auc <- fmt(metrics$auc)
metrics$ks <- fmt(metrics$ks)
metrics$brier <- fmt(metrics$brier)
kable(metrics, caption = "Test-set performance on the locked split. The Python champion row is the published reference from credit-risk-lab.")
```

Verdicts by the frozen rules:

```{r}
#| label: verdicts
data.frame(
  hypothesis = c("H1", "H2", "H3"),
  verdict = c(verdicts$H1$verdict, verdicts$H2$verdict,
              verdicts$H3$verdict)
) |> kable()
```

H1 asked whether the R GBM AUC lands within 0.01 of the Python champion's
0.7810. H2 asked whether the GAM loses no more than 0.02 AUC against the
GBM. H3 asked whether at least one protected attribute shows an
equal-opportunity gap above 5 percentage points at the champion
threshold.

The GAM's smooth terms (effective degrees of freedom and significance)
are in `results/gam_terms.csv`, with the full mgcv summary in
`results/gam_summary.txt`.

# Fairness audit

The audit runs on the R GBM arm at the frozen champion threshold 0.2293
(approve if and only if predicted PD is at or below 0.2293, the study
cut-off recorded in credit-risk-lab). Flagged means predicted PD above
the threshold. TPR is the share of actual defaulters flagged; PPV is the
share of flagged accounts that default; selection rate is the share
approved.

```{r}
#| label: fairness-table
fair$event_rate <- fmt(fair$event_rate, 3)
fair$tpr <- fmt(fair$tpr, 3)
fair$ppv <- fmt(fair$ppv, 3)
fair$selection_rate <- fmt(fair$selection_rate, 3)
kable(fair[, c("attribute", "group", "n", "defaults", "event_rate",
               "tpr", "ppv", "selection_rate")],
      caption = "Per-group fairness table, R GBM arm, locked test set, threshold 0.2293.")
```

```{r}
#| label: gaps-table
gaps$equal_opportunity_gap_pp <- fmt(gaps$equal_opportunity_gap_pp, 2)
gaps$predictive_parity_gap_pp <- fmt(gaps$predictive_parity_gap_pp, 2)
kable(gaps, caption = "Gap summary by attribute, percentage points.")
```

# Claims ceiling

This is a study on public Taiwan 2005 data. It evidences method only:
reproducing a published pipeline in a second language and auditing its
group fairness on the same split. It is not production experience, not a
Canadian portfolio result, and not a claim about any real lender. The
societal stake it speaks to is fair access to credit in Canada: a
champion model whose errors fall unevenly on protected groups is a
finding about the model, and it matters most exactly where credit
decisions gate people's lives.
